title: Microstructure, Mechanical, and Corrosion Properties of 304 Stainless Steel-H13 Tool Steel Composite Cold Spray Coatings

preSprayedProperties.Powder_Morphology: mostly spherical with porous and rough surface due to the dendritic structure. some satellite particles.
preSprayedProperties.Powder_Particle_Size_Other: powder had asymmetrical size distribution, skewed to smaller particless.
preSprayedProperties.Substrate_Surface_Preparation: pre-deposition powder blast at 4.14 MPa and 50°C using the depositing powders (304 and H13)

experimentalProperties.Spraying_System_Model: VRC Raptor high pressure cold spray system
experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: The samples were prepared using standard metallurgical polishing procedures and the final polishing was perform using 0.06 μm diameter colloidal silica for 8 minutes. Electrolytic etching was performed using a DC power supply and 10% oxalic acid. Samples were etched at 6 V and 0.5 A for 20 s to reveal the microstructure.

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: presence of cellular dendritic structure with equiaxed subgrains, which resembles the microstructure of the as received 304 powder. and shows the presence of elongated subgrains. presence of austenite phase.

preSprayedProperties.Powder_Morphology: mostly spherical with porous and rough surface due to the dendritic structure. some satellite particles.
preSprayedProperties.Powder_Particle_Size_Other: average H13 size was 58.0 μm, and its d10, d50, and d90 values were 31.6 μm, 46.9 μm, and 82.0 μm resp. both powders had asymmetrical size distributions. 304 skewed to smaller particles and H13 skewed to larger particles.
preSprayedProperties.Substrate_Surface_Preparation: pre-deposition powder blast at 4.14 MPa and 50°C using the depositing powders (304 and H13)

experimentalProperties.Spraying_System_Model: VRC Raptor high pressure cold spray system
experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: The samples were prepared using standard metallurgical polishing procedures and the final polishing was perform using 0.06 μm diameter colloidal silica for 8 minutes. Electrolytic etching was performed using a DC power supply and 10% oxalic acid. Samples were etched at 6 V and 0.5 A for 20 s to reveal the microstructure.

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: ~90% of the H13 rebounded, leaving only ~10% in the deposit. presence of both austenite and martensite phases, but no good correlation was observed between martensite phase content and H13 tool steel content present in the coatings.

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: ~90% of the H13 rebounded, leaving only ~10% in the deposit. contains few regions with equiaxed subgrains, instead being dominated by the presence of elongated subgrains, which shows improved plastic deformation. presence of both austenite and martensite phases, but no good correlation was observed between martensite phase content and H13 tool steel content present in the coatings.
